overview:
NY-25 is a Democratic-leaning Rochester-area district where Joseph Morelle is seeking another term. The seat carries a double-digit Democratic partisan lean, and Morelle enters the general election as the renominated incumbent. Virginia McIntyre, the Republican nominee, has run a minimal campaign financially.

The resource gap is stark: Morelle has raised about $1.8 million and benefits from outside support on his side, while McIntyre has raised roughly $32,000 with no outside spending directed against the incumbent. No public general-election polls are available and no expert raters have listed the race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals. Prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 97%. With the district's lean, incumbency, and financial advantages all aligned, the race is rated Safe Democratic, with the main uncertainty coming from the absence of polling.
